stem: The names of many drugs used in medicine often include parts of the names of the functional groups their molecules contain.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest two functional groups present in a molecule of the drug named chloramphenicol.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The drug named ketamine readily reacts with protons as shown.

$$\text{ketamine} + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow [\text{ketamine-H}]^+$$

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: State the role of ketamine in this reaction.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Ketamine gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNPH).

Suggest the functional group in the ketamine molecule responsible for this observation.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The mass spectrum of ketamine is determined. Two peaks close to the molecular ion peak, M, are observed with the relative abundances shown in the table.

| peak | $m/e$ | relative abundance |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $M$ | 237 | 100.0 |
| $M+1$ | 238 | 14.3 |
| $M+2$ | 239 | 33.3 |

Use the numbers in the table to show that there are 13 carbon atoms in a ketamine molecule.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
In addition to carbon and hydrogen atoms, each molecule of ketamine contains one atom of each of three different elements. These are called heteroatoms. One of these heteroatoms is a halogen.

Use the figures in the table to suggest the identity of this halogen. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text:
Another peak in the mass spectrum of ketamine has an $m/e$ value of 240.

Predict the relative abundance of this peak.

parts.label: (b)(vi)
parts.text:
Use the information in (b) to complete the molecular formula of ketamine by working out the identities of the three different heteroatoms and the number of hydrogen atoms present.

$$\text{C}_{13}\text{H}$$

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Suggest the number of peaks in the carbon-13 NMR spectrum of neramexane.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The proton ($^1\text{H}$) NMR spectrum of neramexane in $\text{CDCl}_3$ shows five peaks with the following chemical shifts ($\delta$).

| $\delta/\text{ppm}$ | number of protons responsible | splitting pattern (singlet, doublet, triplet, quartet or multiplet) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0.9 |  |  |
| singlet |  |  |
| 1.2 | 3 |  |
| 1.4 | 2 |  |
| 1.7 | 4 |  |
| 2.2 |  |  |
| broad singlet |  |  |

Complete the table.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
Use the Data Booklet and the table in (c)(ii) to complete the assignment of the correct $\delta$ values to each of the circled hydrogen atoms on the structure of neramexane.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text:
One of the peaks in the proton ($^1\text{H}$) NMR spectrum disappears when the sample is shaken with $\text{D}_2\text{O}$.

Identify the peak and explain why it disappears.
